procedure.tool: python tools/cutout_white_background.py (committed, reproducible from the archived originals)
steps: Convert to RGB; per-pixel white distance = max(255-r, 255-g, 255-b).
Flood fill from the four borders where distance <= 8: only background connected to the border becomes transparent, so enclosed cream highlights survive.
Edge ramp: alpha = ((distance - 8) / 14) ** 0.85 for pixels with distance < 22; ramp below 26/255 snaps to 0.
De-fringe: recover subject colour C = (P - (1-alpha)*255) / alpha for partially transparent edge pixels, clamped to 0..255, so downscaling leaves no white halo.
Crop to the alpha bounding box, centre into a square with 5.5% padding per side, resample to 1024x1024 with LANCZOS; no colour edits.
procedure.verification: previews on a checkerboard showed no residual white fringe; opaque/transparent shares above; interior pure-white pixels kept as subject: 0 (coin), 83 (carcass)

notes: Both cards previously used procedural-solid-label placeholders (card.corpse v1 color #284c57, card.coin v1 color #756439); manifest versions bumped to v2 with show_label=false. Load failure still falls back to the old solid colour plus label text.
